description_en: Nexon's game museum in Jeju City reopened in May 2026 after a full renovation. The old computer-history museum is now a hands-on space about players and Nexon's online games, with playable arcade and co-op zones, a retro PC gaming archive, and a MapleStory-themed café in the basement.
opening_hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:30; Café MapleStory last order 17:30)
closed_days: Mon; Seollal (Lunar New Year's Day); Chuseok day
admission_note: Adult 14,000 / teens (middle & high school) 12,000 / children (36 months-grade 6) 10,000 KRW. Seniors 65+, people with disabilities, veterans, military, police and firefighters get 3,000 KRW off with valid ID. Caregiver of a visitor with a severe disability enters free. Jeju residents get 3,000 KRW off. No reservation needed; buy tickets on site. Same-day re-entry is allowed. The B1 café can be used without a ticket.
terrain: indoor building (B1 café + 1F-3F exhibitions), elevator, step-free per VisitJeju
notes: RENAMED: The museum was 넥슨컴퓨터박물관 (Nexon Computer Museum) until it closed on 2026-01-01 for renovation. It reopened as 넥슨뮤지엄 (Nexon Museum) on 2026-05-12. VisitJeju's Korean title is already 넥슨뮤지엄, but its English page still says 'Nexon Computer Museum'. The old domain (computermuseum.nexon.com) redirects to nexonmuseum.org. Hours, prices and address come from the official site's visitor-info text in its JS bundle, plus the footer ('화-일 10:00-18:00, 매주 월요일, 설, 추석 당일 휴관'). The adult price went up from 8,000 to 14,000 KRW. The road address is unchanged; the jibun 노형동 86 matches the source data. Visitors can link a Nexon account for a personalized tour, and the museum suggests installing the Nexon Play app beforehand because kiosk sign-up is slow. The avg_stay figure of 120 min is an estimate: Inven reports visitors now plan 2-3 h, up from about 1 h before. ACCESSIBILITY: VisitJeju lists 단독접근가능, 단차없음, 시각장애인 접근성, 장애인 화장실, 승강기, 장애인 전용 주차장, 수동 휠체어 대여 가능, with assistance-need level '쉬움'. has_stairs=false means the visitor route is step-free per VisitJeju; the building itself does have stairs. Seating: news coverage says the 2F 'Save the Game' documentary is meant to be watched from seats. The official site itself has no accessibility section. The image is a 2014 exterior photo that still shows the old 'Nexon Computer Museum' signage, which may have changed in the 2026 rebrand.

description_en: A huge open-air park and museum complex in the mid-mountain forest of Jocheon, dedicated to Jeju's volcanic stone culture and the island's creation myth of Seolmundae Halmang and her 500 sons. Walking routes link a sunken stone museum, outdoor stone-statue fields, a re-created thatched-roof village, and the Seolmundae Halmang Exhibition Hall that opened in 2025.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales close 17:00); no seasonal change listed
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, closed the next non-holiday day instead); Jan 1; Seollal day; Chuseok day; may also close temporarily for exhibit changes or bad weather
admission_note: Adult (25-64) 5,000 KRW (4,500 online by the day before; 4,000 group of 10+). Youth (13-24) and military/police 3,500 KRW. Age 12 and under free. Age 65+ free, but the official page excludes foreigners from this. Registered people with disabilities free, plus one caregiver for a severe disability. Optional EV shuttle: adult 5,000 KRW.
terrain: large outdoor site in forest/grassland; paved walking paths with stone exhibits on gravel beside them; several indoor halls, some below ground level (B2-1F)
notes: Hours, closed days and prices come from the official visitor guide page; a few third-party listings wrongly say it is open all year. Phone numbers: main line 064-710-7732~3, ticket office 064-710-7764~5, guide booking 064-710-7762. VisitJeju lists the jibun as 교래리 산 95; the source data says 산 119. The road address 남조로 2023 is consistent everywhere. Zone walking times from the official course page: Stone Museum zone about 50 min / 970 m; outdoor exhibition about 50 min / 970 m; thatched village about 40 min / 1,080 m; Seolmundae Halmang Hall about 120 min / 1,800 m; 500 Generals Gallery about 50 min / 900 m. The zones overlap, so avg_stay of 150 min is an estimate for a partial visit. An EV shuttle runs about every 20 minutes with priority boarding for mobility-impaired visitors (per mom-mom.net, not checked on the official page). ACCESSIBILITY: VisitJeju lists 단차없음, 시각장애인 접근성, 장애인 화장실, 장애인 전용 주차장, 수동 휠체어 대여 가능. However, its assistance-need level is '아주 어려움' (very difficult), and the site is very large and spread out. That is why wheelchair_ok is 'partial' and has_stairs is null: the official site does not describe the terrain or stairs. Seating: the official course page lists roofed pavilions and restrooms among the amenities, and the convenience page lists a rest area (쉼팡) and cafés. The 2025 Seolmundae Halmang Hall has a nursing room and first-aid room per VisitJeju.

description_en: Jeju's largest traditional market, held only every five days near the airport, with about 1,000 stalls selling produce, fresh seafood, tangerines, local snacks and household goods. Locals do their real shopping here, and there is a section where elderly women sell their own produce rent-free.
opening_hours: Market days only, approx. 08:00-18:00 (per Korea Tourism Organization data); some guides say stalls close around 19:00. Mornings are busiest.
closed_days: Opens ONLY on dates ending in 2 or 7: the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of each month, whatever the weekday. Closed (no market) on all other dates. Holiday exceptions (e.g., Seollal/Chuseok) not confirmed.
admission_note: Free entry; pay per purchase. Free parking available.
terrain: flat paved ground; large grid of roofed market aisles plus open-air areas; very crowded on market days
notes: Name variants: 제주시민속오일시장 (Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) and the entrance sign), 제주민속오일시장 (VisitJeju), 'Jeju City Traditional 5-Day Market' (VisitJeju English). No official market website was found, so official_url is null. Hours 08:00-18:00 come from KTO data relayed by koreacharts; KTO also says '연중무휴', which only makes sense on market days. Trazy says it closes about 19:00. Market day rule from VisitJeju: '장날 : 매월 2일, 7일, 12일, 17일, 22일, 27일'. There is no market on the 31st or on other dates. Example: 2026-11-11 is not a market day; the next ones are 11/12 and 11/17. Whether it opens when a market day falls on Seollal or Chuseok was not confirmed. The Commons photo (taken July 2026) shows the entrance gate and roofed aisles, hence indoor='mixed'. ACCESSIBILITY: VisitJeju lists only 단차없음 and 수동 휠체어 대여 가능 (manual wheelchair rental), plus 화장실, 공용주차장 and 임산부 휴게시설. No accessible restroom or accessible parking is listed, so accessible_restroom is null. wheelchair_ok is 'partial' because the ground is step-free but aisles get very crowded on market days. Seating was not confirmed. avg_stay of 90 min is an estimate.

description_en: A city-run nature park on the slopes of Geochin Oreum in Bonggae-dong where Jeju's wild roe deer live in the open. A fenced viewing area and small exhibition hall near the entrance make it easy to see deer up close, and a longer forest trail loops around the oreum with views toward Hallasan.
opening_hours: Exhibition hall & permanent observation area (상시관찰원): 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00). Geochin Oreum observation trail: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00); Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00 (tickets until 16:00). Entry may be limited by weather.
admission_note: Adult 1,000 KRW (group of 20+: 800); youth 600 (group 500); age 65+ and age 12 and under free. Deer-feeding experience 1,000 KRW per session (09:00-11:00 and 13:00-16:00), but it is often suspended; check on site.
image_source: Wikimedia Commons, 골뱅이 (via Panoramio), CC BY-SA 3.0
terrain: level area near entrance (exhibition hall, fenced deer enclosure); 2.6 km forest/oreum observation trail around Geochin Oreum with slopes
notes: Run by Jeju City (Jeolmul Ecology Management Office). Hours and fees come from the official 이용안내 page; the fees have applied since 2013-05-01. Conflict: VisitJeju gives the exhibition hall and 상시관찰원 as 09:00-17:00, while the official page says 09:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:00). Several third-party sites give only a flat 09:00-18:00. Today (Nov) is winter season, so the trail closes at 17:00. Closed days: the official page lists none, and KTO/VisitJeju say open year-round. Deer feeding: VisitJeju says it is 'temporarily suspended', and the official site posted a suspension notice for 11/4-11/9, so treat it as not guaranteed. Visit length per VisitJeju: oreum course about 50 min plus enclosure and exhibition hall about 30 min, so avg_stay is about 80 min. The trail is listed as 2.6 km (VisitJeju) or forest trail 2.3 km / main trail 3 km (ktriptips/KTO). A visit limited to the enclosure would be walking level 1 and fatigue about 1-2. ACCESSIBILITY: VisitJeju lists 단독접근가능, 단차없음, 장애인 화장실, 장애인 전용 주차장, with assistance-need level '어려움' (difficult). The 상시관찰원 is explicitly designed for elderly visitors and others who cannot walk far (official facility page). The oreum trail is not described as accessible, hence wheelchair_ok 'partial' and has_stairs null. Restrooms and pavilion rest areas along the trail are listed on the official course and facility pages. KTO says a stroller rental exists, but mom-mom says there is none (conflict, unverified). Free parking. The Commons image shows the entrance sign stone (about 2011).

description_en: Jeju City's oldest downtown shopping street, once nicknamed Jeju's 'Myeong-dong', lined with clothing and shoe brand shops, cafés and small eateries. Part of it is a car-free pedestrian street, and it sits a short walk from Dongmun Market and Tapdong seafront.
opening_hours: Street always open; shop hours vary (roughly 10:00 to 18:00-22:00 depending on the shop)
closed_days: none (street open year-round; individual shops set their own days off)
admission_note: Free to walk; pay per purchase.
image_source: 비짓제주 VISIT JEJU (제주관광공사) 제공 사진 - 공공누리 등 개방 라이선스 표시 확인 안 됨
terrain: flat paved pedestrian street (car-free section about 360 m); some shop entrances have a few steps
notes: Name variants: VisitJeju Korean '제주칠성로상가', English 'Jeju Chilseong-ro Shopping Street'; also 칠성로 쇼핑거리 / 칠성통 / 칠성로상점가. Address conflict: VisitJeju gives 관덕로13길 12 (jibun 일도1동 1476-20, postcode 63277); the source data says 일도일동 1492-1; Trazy says 중앙로7길 15; Hotels.com says 중앙로5길. It is a street, so there is no single official address. The car-free section is 관덕로11길 (from Kumkang Shoes to Tapdong), about 360 m. For taxis, saying '칠성로 쇼핑거리' or 'Chilseong-ro, near Dongmun Market' works better than a street number. The phone 064-721-0827 is from VisitJeju and is probably the merchants' association (unconfirmed). Hours are not official. Trazy says shops close one by one around 22:00. A 2024 Money Today report quotes a long-time shopkeeper now working about 10:00-18:00, and says about 25% of units (77 of 310) were vacant in July 2024, so the street is quieter than older guides suggest. The '칠성로아케이드' name in the source data suggests a covered arcade section, but no current source confirmed a roof, so indoor='mixed' only reflects that the shops are indoors. ACCESSIBILITY: VisitJeju lists 화장실, 공용주차장 and card/cash payment, but no disabled facilities. Its assistance-need level is '아주 어려움' (very difficult), which contrasts with the flat paved street, so wheelchair_ok and has_stairs are null. The VisitJeju photo shows some shop entrances raised by steps. IMAGE: no Commons photo of the Jeju street exists (Commons 'Chilseong' results are all Daegu). The VisitJeju CDN image (.webp, 1242x900) was fetched and loads. Its reuse license is not stated on the page, so confirm 제주관광공사 terms before public use.
